definitions.explanation: In the folk tale of Momotaro, the island where the ogres live and from which Momotaro brings back their treasure.

examples.japanese: ⟦{桃太郎|ももたろう}→桃太郎：30946_momotarou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{鬼|おに}ヶ{島|しま}⟦へ→へ：02473_he⟧{鬼退治|おにたいじ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}った→行く：00119_iku⟧。
examples.english: Momotaro went to Onigashima to defeat the ogres.

examples.japanese: ⟦{犬|いぬ}→犬：00632_inu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{猿|さる}→猿：02213_saru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{雉|きじ}→雉：23161_kiji⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{連|つ}れて→連れる：01240_tsureru⟧、⟦{桃太郎|ももたろう}→桃太郎：30946_momotarou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{鬼|おに}ヶ{島|しま}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{向|む}かった→向かう：01186_mukau⟧。
examples.english: Taking a dog, a monkey, and a pheasant with him, Momotaro set off for Onigashima.

examples.japanese: ⟦{鬼|おに}→鬼：02184_oni⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{退治|たいじ}した→退治する：25396_taijisuru⟧⟦{桃太郎|ももたろう}→桃太郎：30946_momotarou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{鬼|おに}ヶ{島|しま}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{宝物|たからもの}→宝物：12269_takaramono⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}ち{帰|かえ}った→持ち帰る：04227_mochikaeru⟧。
examples.english: After defeating the ogres, Momotaro brought their treasure back from Onigashima.

notes:
Also written {鬼|おに}が{島|しま}; the ヶ is read が.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鬼|おに}ヶ{島|しま}⟦へ→へ：02473_he⟧{鬼退治|おにたいじ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧: to go to Onigashima to fight the ogres (the stock phrase of the tale)
- {鬼|おに}ヶ{島|しま}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{宝物|たからもの}→宝物：12269_takaramono⟧: the ogres' treasure

CULTURAL NOTE:
Every Japanese child knows the story of ⟦{桃太郎|ももたろう}→桃太郎：30946_momotarou⟧. {女木島|めぎじま} in Kagawa Prefecture promotes itself as the original Onigashima, with a large cave said to be the ogres' lair.
